input: head is None or a list head. Each nonempty input is a finite, acyclic singly linked list of caller-supplied nodes with ordinary data fields val and next. val contains plain Python int values, excluding bool; next is another node or None. next fields are writable and nodes within a list are distinct. Accessors, proxies, custom attribute behavior, concurrent observation or mutation during the call, and malformed links are outside the domain. Inputs must fit both runtimes. External caller references to individual nodes are allowed. Preconditions are not checked at runtime.
return: The head of the list with each consecutive pair of original nodes exchanged: positions 1, 0, 3, 2, and so on in zero-based input order. An unpaired final node stays last. The empty input returns None and a singleton returns that same node.
mutation_aliasing: Relinks original next fields to exchange adjacent nodes rather than exchanging their values. All original node identities, values and other fields are preserved; no input node is copied, dropped or replaced. Each original node appears exactly once in the acyclic output, whose tail next is None. Caller-held aliases to nodes observe the changed next graph; the caller's head reference binding itself is not reassigned. One local sentinel is allocated but never returned or linked from any input node. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: The paired domain restricts node values to exact integers in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991], excluding booleans, negative zero, NaN, infinities and BigInt. Python uses plain int and JavaScript uses Number. Values are never read or modified; only node references are inspected and assigned. No list-length counter, bitwise coercion or recursion depth is used.
complexity: O(n + 1) time and O(1) auxiliary space for n input nodes. Each iteration swaps one previously unprocessed pair and advances before to its new tail. One sentinel and a constant number of borrowed references are charged. There is no recursion, collection of node references, node copying or value arithmetic. Field access and reference assignment are constant cost.

helpers.name: Link
helpers.contract: A local sentinel-only class whose constructor stores the supplied next_node reference, defaulting to None, in its sole instance data field next. It does not read, copy or construct caller ListNode objects and has no val field. Sentinels never become nodes in the returned list.
helpers.cost: One constructor call allocates one sentinel object, each in O(1) time and O(1) space. The complete 82-byte UTF-8 helper definition, from class Link through its final definition newline, is byte-identical in 0021.py, 0024.py and 0086.py, and is fully charged in every standalone candidate. Separator newlines are charged in total source bytes.

source_accounting: The complete standalone candidate is 541 UTF-8 bytes, including the 82-byte Link helper, input-shape comment, separator newlines, Solution wrapper, method, constructor calls and terminal newline. Caller ListNode is an explicit input shape, not an uncharged dummy-node constructor: all allocated sentinels use the fully included Link implementation. Shared helper spelling is not a free library. There are no imports, generated source or hidden expansion. Any eventual judge adapter is additional charged source.
evidence_boundary: Independently authored dev_fit candidate outside frozen source sets. No candidate execution, predecessor equivalence, behavioral qualification, benchmark acceptance or M1 progress is claimed. The mandatory isolated judge is unavailable; AST parsing, JavaScript syntax and metadata checks do not establish runtime correctness. Independent source-bound qualification must compare value order, mapped original node identities and the complete post-call next graph, including caller aliases and terminal null links, not just serialized values. Empty, singleton, duplicate-value and odd/even-length inputs plus declared ordering boundaries require qualification before promotion.
